clocks.label: G20 ASHEVILLE
clocks.why: Bessent hosts G20 finance ministers on US soil and demands members sever business ties with Iran or face secondary designation. This clock prices GEO-010 and GEO-011: whether the siege gets multilateral cover, or stays a unilateral instrument that Bloomberg already reports the world is mostly shrugging off.

clocks.label: SCO BISHKEK
clocks.why: Day two of the summit that put Putin, Xi, Modi, Pezeshkian and Erdogan in one hall. It prices whether Brzezinski's antihegemonic coalition can produce a named instrument - a settlement mechanism, a funded facility, a defence clause - or a twenty-sixth communique.

clocks.label: KHARG FALSIFIER
clocks.why: Thirty days from Trump's AI 'smithereens' post. If the loading terminals are actually struck inside this window the video was a warning order and GEO-001, GEO-003 and GEO-009 all re-rate together; if they are intact on Oct 1 it was free coercion and we score that read as confirmed.

clocks.label: RU FUEL EXPORT BAN
clocks.why: Moscow's ban on most diesel, gasoline and jet exports, imposed July 8 and now weighed for a second extension. Each extension publicly admits how much refining Ukraine's drones have taken offline - and removes product from a world market where Hormuz is still restricted.

clocks.label: IRAN-OMAN WINDOW
clocks.why: The 30-60 day technical-talks clock from the Muscat corridor framework. Sunday's minelaying claim landed inside it. If it lapses with no verified minesweeping calendar and no corridor coordinates, the seventh near-breakthrough-then-condition cycle completes.

clocks.label: XI SUMMIT
clocks.why: The state visit GEO-006 (85%) and GEO-012 (29%) both hang on. If a Hormuz concession appears only in the thirty days AFTER it, the leverage-play read is confirmed; if it appears before, the read is wrong.

clocks.label: US MIDTERMS
clocks.why: The master clock every captured file is priced against. Pump prices above $4, casualties and endless-war branding all bill on this date - it is why deferral beats settlement, and why a visible retreat before it is the falsifier on the coalition-capture hypothesis.

speculation.obs: gCaptain, working from Kpler and Vortexa vessel-tracking data, reported that just two commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday 24 August - one very large gas carrier and one very large crude carrier - the lowest daily tally since early May, against a ten-day average of 14 and seven vessels of all types the day before. Vortexa put that day’s oil transit at about 5 million barrels a day against a seven-day moving average of 6 to 7 million as of 23 August.
speculation.src: gCaptain, 25 Aug 2026, citing Kpler and Vortexa ship-tracking data; Vortexa analyst Xavier Tang quoted
speculation.read: Labelled inference, not fact: two hulls in a day is not a corridor, it is a formality. If the counts hold, the useful thing they establish is a floor rather than a trend - a number low enough that it can be moved by a single convoy decision, which means transit tallies are now measuring escort policy more than they measure demand. That matters for reading any announcement of reopening: a jump from two to twenty would tell you the US Navy changed a rule, not that Iran changed its mind. It is also the denominator against which this weekend’s exchange of fire should be judged.
speculation.falsifier: A sustained run of daily transits back into double digits, with oil throughput above 7 million barrels a day, would mean the escort arrangement is functioning and the floor was temporary. Continued single-digit days through September confirms the corridor is nominal.

speculation.obs: Maritime-intelligence firm Windward reported that all three loading terminals at Kharg Island - the terminal through which the overwhelming majority of Iranian crude normally leaves - had been empty for extended runs as of 9 August: the western terminal for 22 consecutive days since 18 July, the LPG terminal for 13 days since 27 July, the eastern terminal for 10 days since 30 July. Vortexa recorded zero departures between 31 July and 9 August, and the waiting area held 17 stationary tankers with their AIS transponders off.
speculation.src: Windward Maritime AI blog, 9 Aug 2026, with Vortexa departure data
speculation.read: Labelled inference: an empty berth is one of the few facts in this theatre that cannot be announced away, because a jetty either has a hull alongside it or it does not. If the run of empty days is right, the interesting number is not the shortfall but the 17 dark tankers parked outside it - that is loaded-and-waiting capacity, or capacity waiting to load, sitting where a satellite can count it. Iran’s export halt would then be a queue rather than a collapse, which matters because a queue clears in days once a corridor opens and a collapse does not. Treat the three-week age of this observation as the main caveat; it is a baseline, not today.
speculation.falsifier: Fresh imagery or Vortexa data showing hulls back alongside the Kharg terminals, with departures resuming, would date-stamp the halt as over. Terminals still empty into September, with the dark waiting-area count rising, would mean the storage-afloat problem is compounding.

speculation.obs: Windward tracked eight sanctioned Russian shadow-fleet tankers moving as a coordinated convoy through the Northern Sea Route toward the Laptev Sea in late July and early August - four Russia-flagged Aframaxes, three Russia-flagged Medium Range tankers and one Oman-flagged Suezmax - loaded at Murmansk and Primorsk between 13 and 22 July with cargoes of roughly 700,000 to 1 million barrels each, several signalling China as destination. The Center for High North Logistics recorded 34 tankers using the route in all of 2025.
speculation.src: Windward Maritime AI blog, 9 Aug 2026; route baseline from the Center for High North Logistics
speculation.read: Labelled inference: eight hulls in one convoy against a 34-hull annual baseline is not a shipping story, it is a routing decision. If the count holds, Russia is testing whether the Arctic can carry sanctioned barrels to Asia outside the insurance, chokepoint and inspection regimes that police the Baltic and Suez routes - a lane with no Danish strait to be boarded in and no Hormuz to be closed. That is the physical fact sitting underneath Lavrov’s complaint today that NATO activity in the Arctic is a direct threat to Russia: the alliance is moving into the region where Moscow is building its sanctions bypass, and the ice window that makes the bypass usable is only a few weeks long.
speculation.falsifier: A second convoy of comparable size before the ice window closes in October, or Chinese customs data showing Arctic-routed Russian crude arriving, would confirm the lane is being industrialised. A single passage with no repeat, or the convoy dispersing short of the Laptev, would mean it was an experiment.

speculation.obs: Open-source imagery analyst MenchOsint posted a Sentinel-2 satellite frame dated 27 August 2026 showing a Kuwaiti Aframax oil tanker sitting idle in the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz after being struck by the IRGC Navy, with a second, smaller boat alongside it - read by the analyst as an attempt to take off the crew. UKMTO had reported a tanker disabled by an attack in the strait on the evening of 26 August, and the incident was picked up by trade press.
speculation.src: @MenchOsint on X (Sentinel-2 imagery); underlying strike reported by UKMTO and Seatrade Maritime
speculation.read: Labelled inference, not fact: the strike itself is corroborated by UKMTO and trade press, so what the imagery adds is the aftermath - a hull still afloat and stationary in the southern channel a day later, with a boat alongside. If that read holds, the IRGC is disabling rather than sinking, and those are different campaigns. A disabled tanker parked in a traffic lane is a durable advertisement that the corridor is conditional, and it costs Tehran far less in escalation than a hull on the bottom. The duller alternative is simply that the weapon underperformed. Either way this is the class of evidence that matters most while transponders are unreliable, because a satellite does not care whether AIS is switched on.
speculation.falsifier: Salvage or a tow, plus an owner or flag-state statement putting damage at the low end, fits the disable-not-sink read. A subsequent strike that actually sinks a hull, or evidence the vessel was simply anchored and undamaged, would break it.

speculation.obs: C4ADS published an ADS-B audit of Russian state and state-linked air traffic into the central Sahel: 75 military or military-linked flights between 1 January 2025 and 31 July 2026, with Burkina Faso used as the intermediate hub, Mali next, and Niger receiving only six. The busiest operator was Flight Unit 224, a Russian defence-ministry airline sanctioned by the US in 2023; the aircraft were mostly Il-76TDs. C4ADS also places the Africa Corps operation at Airbase 101 in Niamey, the field US forces used until their 2024 withdrawal.
speculation.src: C4ADS, ‘Routes and Ramifications’, published 12 Aug 2026 (FlightRadar24 ADS-B data)
speculation.read: Labelled inference, not fact - and this weekend put it to the test. Six flights in nineteen months is a thin pipe, yet the detachment at the end of it is what Niamey’s base command called when its own soldiers mutinied. If the count is right, the Russian presence that just decided a mutiny is supplied overland through Burkina Faso rather than by a dedicated air bridge into Niger. That cuts two ways and we still do not know which. A small advisory detachment that can hold a capital is cheaper leverage than a garrison and easier to deny; but a guarantor that has now been publicly asked to fight has to start flying, and airlift is the one thing ADS-B makes visible in near-real time. This is the pre-crisis baseline the next month gets measured against.
speculation.falsifier: A visible burst of Flight Unit 224 or Il-76TD movements into Niamey over the next month, above the six-flight run rate, would mark the shift from advisers to garrison. Flat traffic while the junta still holds power would mean the assistance was small, local and mostly political.

dossiers.name: Iran

glance.government: Islamic Republic - a clerical-military hybrid in which the security institutions have been ascendant since the February-May war
glance.leader: Mojtaba Khamenei, Supreme Leader since 8 Mar 2026, not verifiably seen in public for roughly six months; Masoud Pezeshkian president; IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi the operative center
glance.gdp: Roughly $300-390bn nominal depending on source; forecast to contract about 5% in 2026 with inflation near 70% and the rial at a record 2.02m to the dollar
glance.military: About 570,000-610,000 active (IISS puts it near 570,000) plus roughly 350,000 reserves; the IRGC Navy, not the regular navy, holds the strait
glance.influence: Transit rights and mine inventory at Hormuz, anti-ship missiles, Iraqi and Yemeni networks - set against oil revenue the central bank governor himself describes as having fallen to zero

dossiers.summary: Start with the constraint, not the man. Iran is a state whose one convertible asset - the barrel - has stopped moving, which is why its remaining leverage is geographic rather than economic, and why it is spent in advertised doses rather than banked. The desk that decides is the IRGC Navy and the new wartime security committee, not the presidency and not the invisible Leader: Washington routed its own peace offer through career Guard commanders, and Iran's president has said on state television that communicating with Khamenei is very difficult. That produces exactly the behaviour this board keeps recording - a volley at forewarned bases in Jordan that was almost entirely intercepted, mines laid and lanes conditionally cleared, six near-breakthroughs that each end in a restated condition. Prospect theory says a cornered regime gambles, but a regime whose survival runs through an institution that profits from the crisis has an interest in holding the temperature where it can still choose it. The falsifier is a strike that actually kills Americans, or a verified minesweeping calendar with published coordinates - either would show the temperature is no longer being chosen.

concerns: Mine and anti-ship capability at Hormuz is intact and reversible - a cleared lane is a maintenance schedule, not a settlement
Succession is unresolved in practice: an unseen Leader plus an IRGC that answers Washington's messages is a leadership fiction with a real chain of command underneath
Oil revenue near zero against 70% inflation removes the economic off-ramp that would normally price restraint
Escalation is now probabilistic rather than intentional - interception rates, not decisions, separate a message from a casualty event

dossiers.name: Russia

glance.government: Presidential autocracy with a managed legislature; State Duma elections due September 2026
glance.leader: Vladimir Putin - the only decider on the war file; Peskov is a thermostat, not an actor
glance.population: About 144 million (2026 estimate; occupied-territory counting disputed)
glance.gdp: Roughly $2.7tn nominal; the government cut its 2026 growth forecast toward 0.4-1%, with oil and gas revenue reported down more than 25%
glance.military: About 1.3 million active with roughly 2 million reserves; defence spending near 6.3-6.5% of GDP
glance.influence: Sanctioned-barrel logistics including the Arctic route, Africa Corps guarantees in the Sahel, energy leverage over Europe, veto and nuclear status

dossiers.summary: Moscow's constraint is refining and money, not morale. Ukrainian deep strikes have pushed refinery runs to about 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since 2002, and the fuel export ban first imposed in July is being weighed for a second extension - each extension a public admission of how much capacity is offline. The deciding desks are the defence and finance ministries rather than the foreign ministry: the September Duma election and the 6.3-6.5% of GDP the war costs are what price the negotiating posture, which is why the deep pause Peskov announced reads as a bargaining position taken from a front that is still moving at Pokrovsk. Watch where the state chose to spend a scarce asset this weekend - Africa Corps, roughly 200-300 personnel supplied overland through Burkina Faso, was used to save a junta in Niamey, buying an advertisement and incurring an obligation in the same act. The observables that would move this file are not statements but airlift and diesel: Flight Unit 224 traffic above its six-flight run rate, or refinery runs recovering past 4m barrels a day.

concerns: The fuel and refining constraint is the real bind - denial is working where punishment has not, and Kyiv is aiming at exactly that
The announced campaign against Ukraine's grid is punishment by Pape's definition, with a poor historical conversion into concessions
Sahel guarantees now carry a defend-the-palace obligation a 200-300 person detachment cannot scale
September Duma elections and a possible post-election reserve call-up are the domestic clock every diplomatic signal is priced against

dossiers.name: Ukraine

glance.government: Wartime presidential republic under martial law; national elections suspended for the duration
glance.leader: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, constrained by coalition dependence; Rustem Umerov holds both the negotiating brief and the intelligence file
glance.population: About 39.5 million on mid-2026 estimates - wartime displacement makes every figure soft
glance.gdp: Roughly $225bn nominal (2025); the EU agreed a package of about EUR 90bn for 2026-27, funded by market borrowing rather than by seizing the roughly EUR 210bn of frozen Russian assets
glance.military: About 677,000 active on the IISS count; larger figures circulate and are not verified
glance.influence: A deep-strike drone campaign that has taken Russian refining to a 24-year low, the Black Sea corridor, and the political weight of being the coalition's test case

dossiers.summary: Kyiv's constraint is arithmetic - manpower, interceptors and a donor calendar - and it sets the strategy rather than following from it. The one instrument Ukraine owns outright is the drone campaign against Russian refineries, which is denial in Pape's sense and is measurably working; nearly everything else is rented from capitals that vote. That dependence is why the deciding desk is now split between the general staff and a negotiating channel run through Washington, and why Zelenskyy has to say yes to the joint Western plan and no to surrender in the same breath. It also explains Myla: an army under sustained deep strike disperses munitions into settlements, which lowers the odds of losing a depot and raises the odds of a night like Friday's, when 38 people died mostly from what the warehouse contained. The falsifiable claim for the winter is that Russia's fuel constraint shapes Russian behaviour more than blackouts shape Ukrainian negotiating positions - if Kyiv's position visibly softens under grid attack while Moscow's does not under fuel shortage, the model is wrong and we say so.

concerns: The announced Russian campaign against the electricity grid arrives with winter and with air-defence stocks already rationed
Pokrovsk is the axis Moscow names when it explains why it is in no hurry to talk; its fall would be a step change, not a line move
Funding is market-borrowed rather than asset-backed, which puts the money on a European political calendar
Dispersal of munitions into inhabited areas makes mass-casualty events recurrent regardless of anyone's aimpoint

dossiers.name: China

glance.government: Party-state under the most centralized leadership since Mao; a recent command purge reshaped the military timetable
glance.leader: Xi Jinping; Wang Yi carries the foreign file with delegated authority
glance.gdp: About $20.9tn nominal (IMF, 2026); 4.7% growth in the first half against a 4.5-5% target, July exports up 23.9% year on year
glance.military: About 2.0 million active, the largest standing force in the world; announced defence budget in the $280bn range
glance.influence: Buyer of last resort for sanctioned barrels, rare earths and the export machine, coast-guard jurisdiction pressure around Taiwan and the East China Sea, and a summit Washington wants

dossiers.summary: Beijing's constraint this quarter is the calendar, not the doctrine. A state visit on 24 September and a tariff truce expiring in November are both worth more than any concession on Iranian crude, which is why the buying continues while the rhetoric stays defiant - and why Treasury sanctioned an Egyptian bank's UAE branches rather than a Chinese one. An enforcer that keeps picking the cheapest nail is telling you which nail is expensive. The desk to watch is not the foreign ministry but the coast guard and the customs administration: PLA sorties around Taiwan have been declining while jurisdictional assertion has been rising, and that ratchet - salami tactics in Schelling's sense, slices too thin to fight over individually - is the actual instrument. Read the summit as accumulation under cover of detente rather than as a thaw, and keep the discount small: announced head-of-state visits with active staff preparation happen about 90% of the time. The tell that breaks the benign read is a coast-guard action inside the visit window; the tell that breaks the leverage read is a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank before 24 September.

concerns: Coast-guard normalization and seabed mapping are precondition-building around Taiwan, not the event itself
China is the load-bearing leak in the Iran sanctions siege - Mulder's rule is that a siege is only as tight as its leakage path
The tariff truce expires in November, just after the summit, which is where a cheap concession becomes an expensive one
A defiant public line paired with quiet compliance makes intent unreadable from statements; only flows settle it

dossiers.name: Israel

glance.government: Parliamentary democracy; the Knesset dissolved in July and the election is set for 27 October 2026
glance.leader: Benjamin Netanyahu, prime minister; Israel Katz defence minister and the cabinet's designated hawk
glance.gdp: About $720bn nominal on 2026 estimates, with defence spending near 8% of GDP
glance.influence: Air superiority over the Levant, the Washington relationship, and an undeclared nuclear status the state has never confirmed

dossiers.summary: Read every Israeli decision on Iran and Lebanon for the next eight weeks through 27 October. That is the constraint: a prime minister facing an electorate more hawkish on this file than his American patron, with Eisenkot and a Bennett-Lapid formation polling as real alternatives, which makes visible restraint expensive and visible action cheap in precisely the window where Washington needs quiet. The deciding desk is the security cabinet, where Katz's line that Israel will soon be required to act again works as the political floor under any ceasefire rather than as a forecast. On Lebanon the framework still has no agreed third-party verifier, and Fortna's finding is that verifier-less ceasefires hold materially worse - which is why the book carries a live probability on a multi-week campaign instead of treating the current quiet as settled. The falsifier is not a speech but an operation: a strike inside Iran during the Muscat window, or a Lebanon campaign in the fortnight before the vote.

concerns: The 27 October election makes restraint politically expensive exactly while the corridor talks need it
The Lebanon framework has no third-party verifier and the party being disarmed rejects the premise
Settler violence in the West Bank now draws prime-ministerial condemnation but almost no prosecutions - the historical file-closure rate is around 94%
An Israeli strike inside Iran during the Muscat window would kill the corridor track outright

dossiers.name: United States

glance.government: Federal presidential republic; midterm elections 3 November 2026
glance.leader: Donald Trump; Scott Bessent at Treasury, Marco Rubio at State, Kevin Warsh at the Federal Reserve
glance.gdp: Roughly $30tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; PCE inflation 3.7% year on year in July and pump prices above $4 a gallon
glance.military: About 1.34 million active with roughly 770,000 reserve and National Guard; budget in the $900bn range
glance.influence: Dollar clearing and OFAC designations, CENTCOM escort of the strait, and a rate path that prices everyone else's oil bill

dossiers.summary: Washington is running two clocks that now contradict each other. The political clock says no forever war and no $4 gasoline before 3 November, which is why strikes keep being called off and why sanctions are the declared instrument. The monetary clock says a chair who concedes the 2% target during an energy spike surrenders the only asset an inflation-fighting central bank owns, which is why Warsh's Friday remark moved September hike odds to 57%. The deciding desks are Treasury's sanctions shop and the two-year note, not the podium - and they pull opposite ways, because the hawkishness that defends the target also lifts the dollar that makes the barrel dearer for every importer. That is the milkshake configuration, oil and dollar expensive together, and it is how an American inflation decision becomes somebody else's reserve sale, with Japan at 160 yen the cleanest instance. The falsifier on the not-in-a-hurry read is dated and simple: a signed de-escalation or a negotiated Hormuz reopening before the midterms would break the coalition-capture hypothesis outright.

concerns: Enforcement at Hormuz is now a standing commitment - a lane you have to keep clearing is not a victory
A September hike into an oil shock puts the dollar and the barrel up together, billing importers twice
The midterm calendar rewards deferral over settlement, which lengthens the crisis it is meant to contain
Confirmed American casualties would collapse the intercepted-volley equilibrium the whole restraint posture rests on

scenarios.q: What if the Kharg video is a warning order rather than theatre?
scenarios.read: The reason to take it seriously is not the rendering, it is the rehearsal: the US actually bombed Kharg on 13 March, hitting more than ninety military sites on the island while deliberately sparing the oil infrastructure. That restraint was the message - we can reach the terminals and are choosing not to. A threat with a demonstrated capability behind it is the one class of declaratory bluster worth staging. The branch is nonetheless built to fizzle, because striking the export terminals of a country whose oil revenue the central bank already describes as near zero destroys the last thing Washington could offer back in a deal.

stages.s: Within two weeks: an explicit official statement naming the terminals rather than a social post, or a NOTAM/airspace or naval movement consistent with a strike package. Falsifier: no official amplification and the post is left to age.

Within 30 days: an actual strike on Kharg's loading terminals or storage, not its military sites. Falsifier: satellite imagery showing the three terminals undamaged on Oct 1 - the dated falsifier the clocks now carry.

Within 60 days of such a strike: Iranian exports go structurally to zero rather than queued, and Brent breaks above the $100 band barrier on a daily close. Falsifier: GEO-009 resolves inside the band on Sep 24.
By February: the sustained multi-week campaign GEO-003 scores. Most branches die at stage A, and this one is designed to.

scenarios.falsifier: Terminals intact and no official amplification thirty days out kills this branch and confirms the free-coercion read - a head of state moving oil 3 percent with a rendering, which is a finding about the information environment rather than about the war.

scenarios.q: What if the weekly sanctions cadence produces a designation Beijing cannot ignore?
scenarios.read: Bessent has publicly pre-committed to a weekly tempo, which is a different object from a single threat: it converts each week's target choice into a scoreable observation about what Washington will and will not pay for. The mechanism is Farrell and Newman's chokepoint effect, enforced not by OFAC but by foreign banks' compliance desks pre-emptively de-risking. The catch is Drezner's: intensity is not compliance, and every use of the chokepoint teaches targets to build around it - CIPS was clearing roughly $270bn a month by March. Note the asymmetry that caps this branch: the summit on 24 September is worth more to both capitals than any single bank.

stages.s: Through September: designations continue weekly and stay in cheap jurisdictions - Gulf branches, Egyptian, Turkish or Emirati institutions. Falsifier: a week passes with no designation, which would mean the cadence was rhetoric.

Before Sept 24: a designation touching a Chinese entity of any size - a teapot refiner, a port operator, a mid-tier bank - short of a top-ten bank. Falsifier: nothing Chinese designated before the summit.
Before Oct 1: a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank, which is GEO-011 at 7% and would break the hammer-that-hangs read. Falsifier: the summit happens on schedule with the banks untouched.

By December: Chinese purchases of Iranian crude actually halve for two consecutive months - GEO-010 at 12%. This is the stage the sanctions literature says almost never arrives against a great power on a core interest.

scenarios.falsifier: A Chinese top-ten designation before the summit kills the leverage read outright and we mark it as a miss. Equally, two consecutive weeks with no new designation would mean the weekly commitment was a press line and the whole branch collapses at stage A.

scenarios.q: What if Moscow's Sahel guarantee gets called a second time?
scenarios.read: Niger converted an advertisement into an obligation this weekend: a 200-to-300-person Africa Corps detachment supplied overland through Burkina Faso decided who governs a country, and did so publicly at Russia's own ambassador's account. The mechanism is regime-preservation as a service, and its economics are excellent while it is small and terrible if it must scale - a guarantor that has been seen to fight cannot decline the next call without devaluing every other guarantee. The boring alternative deserves equal weight and is named: this was a pay-and-body-bags mutiny by officers from the worst-hit frontline districts, and the junta's supply failure explains it without any external hand.

stages.s: Within a month: a visible airlift response - Flight Unit 224 or Il-76 movements into Niamey above the six-flight-in-19-months baseline. Falsifier: flat ADS-B traffic with the junta still standing, meaning the help was small, local and political.

Within six months: a second coup attempt in Niger or a comparable challenge in Mali or Burkina Faso. Base rate supports it - a first failed attempt materially raises the odds of a second. Falsifier: a quiet half-year across all three.
Within a year: a formalised basing or minerals instrument - the debt collected in access rather than cash, with uranium the file nobody named this weekend. Falsifier: no published agreement.
Beyond: Africa Corps commitments exceed what an overland-supplied detachment can hold and Moscow visibly declines a client. This is where the branch usually dies unremarked.

scenarios.falsifier: Flat airlift, no second attempt and no new instrument within six months would mean the obligation read was overdrawn and the intervention was a cheap one-off - we score that as a miss rather than saying not yet.

quiz.q: CENTCOM says it struck the Larak launchers because the IRGC was preparing rockets carrying sea mines. Why does the brief treat minelaying as the more important half of the board than the missile exchange?
options: Mines are far more lethal to warships than ballistic missiles are
Mines are cheap, deniable and reversible, so they let Iran keep the strait conditional without committing to an attack anyone must answer
Mines are banned under international law and missiles are not
Iran has no missiles left after the February war
quiz.why: A cleared lane is a maintenance schedule, not a settlement. Minelaying is the instrument that keeps Hormuz permanently conditional at almost no escalation cost, which is why the American strike went at launchers on a rock rather than at anything strategic - and why the mine question, not the missile question, sets the Hormuz forecasts.

quiz.q: Brent rose 2.93 percent on a day when the only thing that happened to Kharg Island was a video. What does that tell you about the instrument?
options: The market had inside knowledge of a real strike
A credible threat is priced whether or not it is executed, which makes declaratory coercion cheaper than a strike
Oil markets are irrational and ignore fundamentals
Kharg was in fact hit and the reporting is lagging
quiz.why: Credibility, not execution, is what markets price - and this threat is credible because it was rehearsed on 13 March, when the US bombed Kharg's military sites and deliberately spared the oil infrastructure. That earlier restraint is what makes the current gesture expensive for Iran and free for Washington.

quiz.q: Treasury has now promised WEEKLY secondary designations. Why does our book still put the campaign achieving its stated aim at only 12 percent?
options: Because Treasury lacks the legal authority to designate foreign banks
Because the buyer whose behaviour would decide the outcome - China - keeps not being designated, and sanctions rarely move a great power on a core interest
Because Iran has already agreed to reopen the strait
Because secondary sanctions have never been used before
quiz.why: Mulder's rule is that a siege is only as tight as its leakage path, and Drezner's finding is that sanctions change behaviour about a third of the time at best and near zero against a great power on a core interest. An enforcer that keeps picking cheap jurisdictions is telling you which target it does not intend to hit.

quiz.q: Brzezinski warned in 1997 about exactly the Russia-China-Iran grouping now meeting in Bishkek. What does the brief say is missing before calling it an alliance?
options: A shared border and a common language
Any binding instrument - no mutual-defence clause, no common currency, no joint command
Formal recognition by the United Nations
Enough combined military spending to match NATO
quiz.why: The analysis lives in the gap between the photograph and the instrument. Twenty-five years of SCO summits have produced communiques rather than obligations, and India - buying Russian crude and American weapons at once - is the standing evidence that members are hedging, not committing.

quiz.q: A post from a head of state shows video of an enemy oil terminal exploding. Which single observable would best tell you whether anything actually happened?
options: Whether the country's state media denies it
Whether commercial satellite imagery shows damage to the loading terminals, or tankers resume berthing there
Whether the post is later deleted
Whether oil prices rise on the day
quiz.why: Denials, deletions and price moves are all consistent with both a real strike and a fabricated one - that is what makes them useless as evidence. A jetty either has a damaged structure and no hulls alongside it or it does not, and imagery of the berths is the observable that cannot be announced away.

decode.claim: The United States has entered the biggest oil deal in history, taking majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil, more than doubling American oil reserves, substantially lowering gas prices, and at no cost to the American taxpayer.
decode.source: Trump social-media post, Aug 28; structure briefed by a US official
decode.verdictNote: Framing, and the load-bearing distinction is where reserves are counted. Oil reserves are booked to the ground they sit in, not to the nationality of the shareholder — 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan proven reserves stay Venezuelan reserves under every accounting convention, and what Washington describes buying is 55% of a new company's effective output, split between an equity stake and the right to buy barrels at cost. That is a claim on production, not title. “No cost to the American taxpayer” is also narrower than it sounds: it means no appropriated cash this year, not no sovereign risk on a 100-year concession under an interim government installed after the US removed its predecessor.
decode.reality: Trump announced the deal on social media on Aug 28 and named Marco Rubio, Pete Hegseth and Venezuela's acting president Delcy Rodríguez as the negotiators. A US official describes a joint venture with a private Venezuelan company covering 17 fields, a 100-year lease over 65 billion barrels of proven reserves, and a 55% US share of effective output split between ownership and at-cost purchase rights, with at-cost barrels going to the Strategic Petroleum Reserve and the military. Venezuela is currently producing about 1.23m barrels a day — its highest since February 2019 — of which Chevron's joint venture accounts for roughly 260,000. For scale on the reserves claim: US proved crude and lease-condensate reserves were 46.4bn barrels at end-2023 (EIA), so 65bn is indeed the larger number, which is exactly why adding it across a border is the move worth catching.
decode.aspiration: No agreement text has been published. The private operator has not been officially named (reporting points to Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt). Nobody has said how the 55% divides between equity and at-cost rights, who funds the roughly $100bn of investment Rubio cited, or which sanctions authorisation lets a US government entity hold the stake. Venezuela's constitution treats hydrocarbons as inalienable public domain and no National Assembly ratification has been shown. Chevron and ExxonMobil both declined to comment — no major has committed capital. On prices: energy analysts Amy Myers Jaffe and Kevin Book both say the infrastructure work takes years and billions, and will not move the pump price this weekend.

angles.effect: Gains an energy-price story and a below-market SPR refill before the midterms, bought with an announcement rather than an appropriation — the cheapest possible instrument, and the reason it arrived as a post rather than a treaty.
Converts a transitional mandate into a governing one: recognition, sanctions relief and a promised $100bn of capital, paid for by pre-committing decades of the country's principal asset.

The concession runs through a private company, so operatorship of what a US official called the world's second-largest private oil company by reserves lands with one businessman rather than a state entity — while Chevron and Exxon pay nothing and say nothing, which is the correct position while the legal text, the sanctions carve-out and the arbitration clause are all missing.

angles.party: Venezuelans and any future elected government
angles.effect: Carry the bill. They inherit a contract they did not vote on, and a dilemma: honour it and a century of the resource is spoken for; break it and sanctions and the security question come straight back.

The party absent from the announcement. If Venezuelan heavy sour genuinely reaches Gulf refiners in volume, the Canadian heavy discount widens — Alberta pays part of the price of a Washington announcement and gets no seat in it.

clock.d90: Sentiment, not molecules. Production stays near 1.2–1.3m b/d and there is no measurable pump-price effect. The testable event is the signing session Caracas says is scheduled for next week, and whether a document appears with it.
clock.m18: The capital question resolves. Either an OFAC authorisation and a published contract exist and a major commits real money, or the deal stays a press release with a lease number attached. Watch whether output moves toward the stated 1.5m b/d.
clock.y7: Where 65bn either becomes barrels or does not. Orinoco extra-heavy crude needs upgraders, diluent, power and port capacity that do not exist at the claimed scale today — and this is also where political durability is tested, when a Venezuelan government that did not sign this has to decide whether to honour it.

watch: The published contract text — its governing law and arbitration seat, the legal name of the joint venture and the identity of the private operator. Its absence is currently the single biggest hole in the claim.
An OFAC general licence or amended sanctions authorisation covering the venture — without one, no US major can lawfully fund it.
A Venezuelan National Assembly ratification vote or gazette publication, given the constitution's inalienable-public-domain clause.
A first at-cost cargo delivered into the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, with a dated bill of lading and the price paid versus market.
Venezuelan monthly production in OPEC secondary-source figures crossing 1.5m b/d.
decode.easy: The president said America now controls 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's oil, that it costs you nothing and that it will lower fuel prices. No signed contract has been published, the oil stays in Venezuelan ground under Venezuelan law, and getting it out takes years — so today this mostly helps the government in Caracas that needs the money and the private company that gets to run the fields.

decode.claim: Venezuela preserves ownership of and sovereignty over its resources under a 25-year agreement that returns $19 from every barrel sold to the US, worth up to $209 billion.
decode.source: Delcy Rodríguez, Venezuela's acting president, televised address
decode.verdictNote: Partly true, and the half that survives matters: Venezuela does keep legal title, because what Washington describes acquiring is a stake in a company plus purchase rights, not ownership of rock. Both governments can be telling the truth about that at the same time. What they cannot both be right about is the term — Caracas says 25 years, Washington says a 100-year lease — and the money does not reconcile either: 1.5m barrels a day at $19 a barrel is roughly $10bn a year, so $209bn is only reachable as a multi-decade cumulative total, not an annual one.
decode.reality: Rodríguez said in a televised address that the deal covers 17 strategic oilfields with an initial production target of 1.5m barrels a day plus eight greenfield blocks, that $19 from every barrel sold to the US flows to Caracas, and that Venezuela retains “ownership of and sovereignty” over its natural resources “while leveraging capital, technology and operational expertise.” She said agreements would be signed the following week. Venezuela's actual output today is about 1.23m b/d, with a government target of 1.37m by year-end — so 1.5m is an increase, not a transformation.
decode.aspiration: The 25-year term is asserted, not documented, and is directly contradicted by the US description of a 100-year lease. The $209bn figure, the $100bn of inbound investment, the eight greenfield blocks and the signing itself are all forward-looking. No text has been published, no National Assembly ratification has been reported, and the constitutional question — whether an inalienable public-domain resource can be committed this way at all — is untouched in her address.

angles.effect: Turns an interim mandate into a sovereignty-preserving national win and gets a fiscal number, $19 a barrel, that she can put in a budget speech. The word 'sovereignty' is doing the political work the term sheet cannot.

angles.party: The PSUV base and the Chavista tradition
angles.effect: Asked to accept foreign operatorship of the industry Chávez nationalised. 'Ownership retained' is the formula that makes that survivable inside the party — which is precisely why it was the first phrase in the address.
Boxed in. Opposing the deal means opposing sanctions relief and $100bn of investment; supporting it means blessing terms negotiated by a government seated after a US operation removed the last one.
Gains by conceding the word. Control of output was always the object, so letting Caracas keep the language of sovereignty costs nothing and stabilises the counterpart it needs to sign.

angles.party: Venezuelan citizens and every government after this one
angles.effect: Pay the spread. They receive $19 a barrel while the venture keeps the rest of the value chain, and they carry the difference between a 25-year commitment and a 100-year one — a gap of three generations that nobody has put in writing, agreed to by an unelected acting president on television.

clock.d90: The signing session Caracas promised. The only thing that matters is whether a stated term appears in a document — 25 or 100 — and whether the National Assembly touches it.
clock.m18: Whether $19-a-barrel receipts actually appear in Venezuelan fiscal accounts, and whether output moves from 1.23m toward the stated 1.5m b/d.
clock.y7: Whether the term survives a change of government in Caracas or of administration in Washington. A concession is paper until an institution enforces it.

watch: The stated term in the signed text — the one number that settles the 25-versus-100-year contradiction between the two announcing governments.
Whether the $19 per barrel is structured as royalty, tax or profit share, and whether it is indexed to price.
A National Assembly ratification vote or publication in the Gaceta Oficial.
A Venezuelan budget line showing receipts from the venture, in the next fiscal presentation.
Whether the eight greenfield blocks appear in the same instrument as the 17 producing fields or in a separate, later one.
decode.easy: Venezuela's acting president said the country keeps ownership of its oil, that the deal lasts 25 years and pays Venezuela $19 a barrel. The ownership part is fair — but Washington described the same deal as a 100-year lease, and the $209 billion she cited only works as a total over decades, not per year.

decode.claim: The violence in the West Bank villages of Qusra and Jalud was criminal, committed by a handful of rioters who are violating the law and harming Israel's standing in the world.
decode.verdictNote: The condemnation is real and unusually direct from this prime minister — but the load-bearing word is “handful,” which recasts a documented and recurring pattern as isolated deviance. The follow-through so far is evidentiary rather than prosecutorial: the military impounded vehicles for a police file, and no arrests were announced. Yesh Din's monitoring of 1,701 police investigations since 2005 finds 93.8% closed with no indictment and only 3% ending in conviction, so a statement and a case file are not the same object.
decode.reality: Dozens of settlers descended on Qusra on Saturday after nearly three weeks of tension, throwing stones at residents and barricading themselves inside a house with Palestinians still in it; in nearby Jalud settlers attacked a Palestinian family and an NBC News crew. The army removed settlers from the Palestinian home, separated the groups, and confiscated vehicles suspected of having been used to reach the area as evidence for a police investigation. Netanyahu's statement was issued the same day and is a rare rebuke.
decode.aspiration: Everything downstream of the words. No arrests were announced, no suspects named, no indictments filed, no administrative orders issued against Israeli citizens for these incidents. Nothing in the statement names an instrument — no policing change, no deadline, no minister tasked. Whether the impounded vehicles produce identified suspects is the open question, and the base rate says most such files close as “offender unknown”.

angles.effect: Buys international cover at zero coalition cost. Words carry no price with his partners; and note the injury he names is to 'the law-abiding Jewish community' and to 'Israel's standing in the world' — the framing is reputational, not about the people who were attacked.
Lose nothing. The statement stops precisely where a coalition fight would begin: it names no policy, no ministry and no enforcement target, so the national-security portfolio is untouched.

Handed an expectation without new authority or a deadline. The statement even describes the army as being 'interfered with' — casting the force responsible for order in the territory as the aggrieved party rather than the accountable one.

angles.party: Residents of Qusra and Jalud, and the reporters covering them
angles.effect: Pay in full and in advance. They face recurring attacks and a 93.8% no-indictment rate, which is the number that actually predicts their next year — not the sentence read out in Jerusalem. An NBC crew was attacked alongside them, and unpunished attacks on journalists mean fewer journalists in those villages, which erodes the evidence base condemnations depend on.

angles.party: European and US officials weighing settler sanctions
angles.effect: Handed the counter-argument. A prime-ministerial condemnation is the strongest available case for holding off on designations — which is a benefit to Israel's government whether or not a single indictment follows.

clock.d90: Whether the Qusra and Jalud files produce named suspects and indictments, or close. This is the only window in which the statement can be falsified cheaply.
clock.m18: Whether the 2026 indictment and conviction rates move off their twenty-year band. One prosecution is an anecdote; a shift in the percentage is a policy change.
clock.y7: Whether any enforcement architecture in Area C changes at all — jurisdiction, police staffing, or the standing of Israeli civilians under military versus civil law.

watch: A named indictment with a case number arising from the Qusra or Jalud incidents.
Whether the impounded vehicles yield identified suspects, or the files close on “offender unknown” — the disposition of those specific vehicles is the cheapest available test.
Any administrative detention or restraining order issued against Israeli citizens for these attacks.
Yesh Din's next data sheet and the 2026 closure and conviction percentages.
Whether the national security ministry publicly backs, contradicts or slow-walks the police investigation.
decode.easy: Israel's prime minister called the settler attacks on two Palestinian villages criminal, which he rarely does. But so far the army has only impounded some cars and nobody has been arrested — and over twenty years, 94 out of every 100 of these police files have closed with no charges at all.

decode.claim: The prompt reaction of Niger's defence and security forces contained the mutiny and gradually regained control of the sites attacked in Niamey.
decode.source: Niger junta statement read on state television
decode.verdictNote: Partly true — and the tell is inside the wording. A government that held its capital does not need to announce that it “gradually regained control” of sensitive sites; the sentence concedes the sites were lost before it claims they were recovered. Containment itself looks real — the state broadcaster came back on air, and the presidential guard repelled an attempt on the palace — but a diplomatic source told AFP the guard retook the air base “with the help of the Russians,” which, if confirmed, means the regime's own forces were not sufficient. That is the part of the day that has consequences, and it is not in the statement.
decode.reality: Sustained gunfire and explosions were reported on Aug 29 around Base 101, the presidential palace and the state broadcaster in Niamey. Soldiers from the Base 101 barracks opened fire on several sensitive sites after attempting to detain fellow soldiers. Télé Sahel went off air for about an hour before being restored around 10:00. Security sources confirmed an attempted breach of the presidential palace was pushed back by the presidential guard. This is the latest challenge to Abdourahamane Tiani, who took power in the 2023 coup.
decode.aspiration: Almost every operational detail. No casualty figures, no confirmed arrests, no confirmation of airport status, no named plotters, and — the absence that matters most — no dated public appearance by Tiani himself. The Russian assistance rests on a single anonymous diplomatic source and has not been confirmed or denied by Niamey or Moscow. “Contained” is a claim about a moving situation made by the party with the strongest interest in it being over.

angles.effect: Survive the day and acquire a licence for a purge of the officer corps — the standard post-mutiny move, and the one that tells you how frightened they actually were. Watch the arrest list, not the statement.

angles.party: The mutineers, reported as junior officers
angles.effect: If they are named and tried publicly, the regime is confident. If the files stay sealed and the men disappear into detention, it is not — secrecy after a failed coup usually indicates the plot reached higher than the government wants known.

angles.party: Russia and its Africa Corps presence
angles.effect: If the air base really was retaken with Russian help, Moscow converts a security service into standing political leverage over Niamey — over uranium contracts, over basing, over what Niger can refuse later. Protection is the most expensive thing a weak government can accept, and France and the US, already expelled from their Niger bases, have no instrument left to compete for it.

angles.party: The Sahel alliance partners, Mali and Burkina Faso
angles.effect: A wobble in Niamey wobbles all three. Their juntas rest on the same arithmetic of junior officers with weapons and grievances, and each attempt raises the perceived odds for the next — as it does for the uranium buyers repricing supply risk who were consulted by nobody.

Pay in curfews, communications cuts and a security establishment that now has to watch itself as well as the jihadist insurgency in Tillabéri — attention diverted from the threat that actually kills them.

clock.d90: Arrests, a military tribunal, and a reshuffle of the general staff or the presidential guard command. Also whether Tiani appears in person, on a dated broadcast — the cheapest proof of control there is.
clock.m18: Whether the purge stabilises the army or seeds the next attempt, and whether any Russian role formalises into a written basing or training agreement.
clock.y7: The base rate governs. Niger has now seen repeated coups and attempts; a regime that survives by purging its officer corps tends to meet the same event again, and each round narrows the pool of officers it can trust.

watch: A published list of arrested officers and the convening of a military tribunal — names and ranks, not a numbered total.
Tiani appearing in person on state television, with a verifiable date.
An official Nigerien or Russian statement confirming or denying Russian participation at Base 101 — the single missing document that would change the read of the whole day.
Reopening of Diori Hamani international airport and a return to published flight schedules.
Changes to the command of the presidential guard or the army general staff in the next gazette.
decode.easy: Soldiers attacked the presidential palace and an air base in Niger's capital, and the government says it contained the mutiny and took the sites back. Saying you “gradually regained control” admits you lost them first — and a diplomatic source says Russian forces helped, which would mean the government now owes Moscow for its own survival.

track.note: Nothing has resolved yet, and we publish that rather than dress it up. All 22 forecasts were checked against their deadlines in the Aug 30 audit and against early resolution - the Brent band is the only one that can resolve early, on a single daily close outside 80-100, and Brent settled 88.29 mid-band. The first real score lands Sep 24, then the Xi summit and the Chinese-bank question on Oct 1. Every score appears here as it happens, the misses first. A track record you can only see after it looks good is not a track record.

plumbing.read: The buffer is gone and the pressure is now in two places at once. ON RRP sits at $0.17B, down 84% on the month - the reverse-repo parking lot that would absorb any drain of short-end support is effectively empty - while the Fed balance sheet quietly expanded 0.8% to $6.73T. On the physical side, the product market is tightening from both ends: Russian refinery runs at a 24-year low with a fuel export ban running past Sept 1, and Hormuz still moving roughly a tenth of its pre-war traffic. What is still NOT printing is the milkshake tape - oil AND dollar expensive together. The broad dollar is soft at 118.1, down 2.4% on the month, and that remains the strongest live evidence against escalation. Pressure in the plumbing, not yet in the price.
plumbing.epoch: E6 still open — the Sept-2019 repo confession never closed — running alongside E7, the weaponized-settlement rail opened by the 2022 reserve freeze that the record official gold bid is a late chapter of.

series.note: the short end the Fed is buying

easy.bottomLine: The president posted a video that looked like Iran's biggest oil island being destroyed. It was made by a computer, and hours later there was still no sign the island had been touched. The real attack was much smaller: America bombed two rocket launchers on a different Iranian island, because it says Iran was getting ready to drop mines in the world's most important shipping lane. Iran fired missiles back at two American bases in Jordan and sent a drone at the UAE, and almost all of it was shot down. Nobody American was killed - but the price of oil went up 3 percent anyway. That is the whole lesson of the day: a fake video moved real money.
easy.risk: Still HIGH, not higher. The shooting restarted but stayed small, and both sides shot at things they knew the other could defend. It gets much worse if Americans are killed, and it calms down if two quiet weeks pass. Elsewhere in the world: Russia's soldiers helped the government of Niger survive an attempt by its own army to overthrow it, the leaders of Russia, China, India, Iran and Turkey all met in one room in Kyrgyzstan, and Nepal's flood death toll has passed 903 with more than 4,000 people still missing.
easy.markets: Oil rose to 90.69 dollars a barrel, up almost 3 percent, mostly on the strike and the threat. American petrol is above 4 dollars a gallon, compared with under 3 when this war started in February. America's Treasury secretary said he will announce new punishments on banks that deal with Iran EVERY WEEK from now on, and called it financial violence. The rest of the world has mostly ignored the threat so far.
brief: The president shared a computer-made video of Iran's main oil island exploding, but the island was not attacked. The real attack was two rocket launchers on a much smaller island, and oil still got 3 percent more expensive.

America's Treasury secretary says he will punish a new bank almost every week for doing business with Iran. He picked an Egyptian bank last week and did not pick a Chinese one, even though China is the country actually buying Iran's oil.
The leaders of Russia, China, India, Iran and Turkey all met in Kyrgyzstan. It looks like a rival team to America, but the group has no army, no shared money and no promise to defend each other.
Soldiers in Niger tried to overthrow their own military government, and Russian troops stationed at the airbase helped stop them. That means the government now owes Russia for staying in power.
A huge piece of glacier fell into a river in Nepal and washed away 72 kilometres of villages. More than 903 people are confirmed dead, over 4,000 are missing, and six power stations were wrecked.

risk.line: Held at HIGH for a second reading, and the reason is worth stating plainly: the shooting resumed but the day's loudest object was not a weapon. President Trump posted AI-generated video captioned “Kharg Island being blown to smithereens”; hours later there was still no evidence Kharg had been touched, and the actual American operation was two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak Island, more than 400 miles down the Gulf, which CENTCOM described as limited and precise and ordered because Guards were readying rockets carrying sea mines for the international lanes. Iran answered with ballistic missiles at two US bases in Jordan — Jordan's military says it intercepted eight — and a drone at the UAE from Iranian waters, which the Emirati air force shot down. No confirmed American dead. Brent settled the argument in the only currency that counts: 90.69 dollars, up 2.93 percent, on a synthetic video and two destroyed launchers. That is free coercion, and it is cheaper than a strike. The second board moved too: Scott Bessent told the AP that new secondary sanctions will now land WEEKLY, called the campaign “financial violence if we have to,” and takes that demand to G20 finance ministers at Asheville on Monday — while again naming another bank, and again not a Chinese one. Off the Gulf board: Putin, Xi, Modi, Pezeshkian and Erdogan convened in Bishkek for the SCO's 25th anniversary; Russia's Africa Corps helped a junta in Niamey survive its own mutinying soldiers; and Nepal's flood toll passed 903 dead with 4,247 missing after a glacier fell into the Trishuli valley.

forecasts.q: Major US/Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes
forecasts.note: RAISED +4, the day's biggest move. The month-long lull broke: the first publicly acknowledged US strike on Iranian territory since late July, Iranian retaliation against TWO third countries (missiles at US bases in Jordan, a drone at the UAE), and a president publicly posting AI video of Kharg - the terminal that ships about 90% of Iranian crude - being destroyed. The reference class here is RECURRENCE, not war initiation, and in that literature the hazard of renewed major fighting is highest immediately after a lull breaks rather than spread evenly across the horizon. Capped at +4 because CENTCOM called it limited and precise, Iran's reply was target-matched and intercepted, and the named November trigger still sits later in the window

That is a physical act inside the technical window, not a statement - the seventh near-breakthrough-then-condition cycle. Fortna's finding anchors it: corridors and ceasefires with no agreed third-party verifier hold materially worse, and there is still no published minesweeping calendar and no corridor coordinates.
