forecasts.q: Economic D-Day works: China cuts Iranian oil >50%, sustained
forecasts.note: Held despite a loud day. Bessent escalated INTENSITY - weekly designations, a G20 demand, financial violence - but Bloomberg reports the world mostly shrugged off the D-Day threat, and Drezner's point is precisely that intensity is not compliance: sanctions change behaviour about a third of the time at best and near zero against a great power on a core interest. The question asks about Beijing, and Beijing was not designated

forecasts.q: US sanctions a top-10 Chinese bank before the Xi summit
forecasts.note: Held at 7, with the two effects named. A weekly cadence adds draws, which pushes up; Bessent again said the next target is another bank and again did not say a Chinese one, which pushes down. Farrell and Newman's rule decides the tie: the hammer that hangs is worth more than the hammer that falls, and an enforcer that keeps picking the cheapest nail is telling you which nail is expensive

forecasts.q: US commits to fixed Venezuelan heavy-crude export infrastructure
forecasts.note: Held under the stricter Aug 30 wording. Chevron expanding Petropiar into the Ayacucho 8 block and a 300,000 b/d export target by March are field-access and offtake items; this question needs an awarded dredging or terminal contract. Motive is untouched - premeditation is what this scores, and concrete is what would show it

forecasts.q: Xi state visit to US happens in September
forecasts.note: Held. Xi is in Bishkek for the SCO summit exactly as the calendar said he would be, which is a small confirmation of the staff-preparation signal rather than new information. Announced head-of-state visits with active sherpa work are consummated about 90% of the time

forecasts.q: IF a Hormuz deal happens, it preserves Iranian transit administration
forecasts.note: Held, and today strengthened the mechanism without moving the number. Ostovar's thesis is that the IRGC converts crisis into permanent institution; an organisation that answers a strike on its minelayers within hours is demonstrating that transit control is its institutional property, not a bargaining chip the foreign ministry can trade

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire holds 30+ days
forecasts.note: Held. Bishkek changes nothing here: about 79% of interstate wars end within two years and Ukraine at 4.5 years is deep in the tail where the odds of stopping get lower, not higher. Summits between belligerents' patrons are not negotiations between belligerents

forecasts.q: Russian Q4 territorial gains fall below the Q2-Q3 average
forecasts.note: Held. Autumn mud then winter have historically depressed mechanized tempo against summer, before Kofman's manpower-crossover argument adds anything. ISW logged no Russian advances in the Novopavlivka and Oleksandrivka directions on Aug 28-29 and no ground activity reported at Pokrovsk on Aug 29 - consistent, not yet evidence

forecasts.q: Mojtaba makes a verified live public appearance
forecasts.note: Held. A day in which Iran's answer to a US strike was announced by the IRGC and its foreign ministry, with no word from the Leader on the most salient security event in a month, is consistent with the invisible-Leader model - but consistency is not new evidence and we do not re-count the same fact

forecasts.q: Fed's standing T-bill purchase program still running at end-2026
forecasts.note: Held. The exit got harder, not nearer: ON RRP at $0.17bn against a balance sheet at $6.73tn means there is no buffer to absorb a drain of short-end support. Facilities persist when the conditions that would justify ending them deteriorate

forecasts.q: Israel-Hezbollah escalates to multi-week campaign
forecasts.note: Held. Fortna is the anchor: ceasefires with an agreed third-party verifier hold materially better, and this framework still has none while the party being disarmed rejects the premise. The Oct 27 Israeli election is the constraint that prices it

forecasts.q: China quarantine or blockade of Taiwan
forecasts.note: Held. Coast-guard normalization and seabed mapping are precondition-building, not the event. Allison is on record at under 1% for a blockade this year; Fravel and Mastro say the command purge pushed the kinetic timetable right

forecasts.q: US-China tariff truce collapses before Nov expiry
forecasts.note: Held. Negotiated truces rarely collapse before their own expiry while both parties are staging a summit inside the window, and the sanctions round that could have broken it named an Egyptian bank instead

forecasts.q: IF Ukraine fighting stops 30+ days pre-2028: armistice, no peace treaty
forecasts.note: Held. Stalemated interstate wars end in armistices far more often than in signed peace treaties - Korea 1953, Iran-Iraq 1988. If anything this is conservative

forecasts.q: Security-elite fracture in Iran (IRGC defection, coup, mass purge)
forecasts.note: Held. The decapitation-survival literature says security elites usually cohere, and a Corps that absorbs a strike and answers it within hours is cohering, not cracking. Takeyh's test needs a verified defection or purge

forecasts.q: China stands up a third physical-gold venue or a delivery-forcing mechanism
forecasts.note: Held. Gold volatility at 26.8, up 8.8% on the month, is stress in the paper market rather than venue construction - the distinction this question was cut for conflating last week. Reference class: two venues in twenty-four years

forecasts.q: Bitcoin's cycle top prints at or below ~$150k
forecasts.note: Held. The adoption-saturation model is untouched by this week's flow. Wide bars - Bitcoin has never traded through a real recession

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (NEW — the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Opens at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — 75% → 82%
hypotheses.d: Week's biggest mover, on three strands independent of the Israeli/exile channel. Pezeshkian said on Iranian state TV that communication with Khamenei is 'very difficult' — Tehran's own president, against his own interest. Washington routed its peace offer not to Araghchi but to Mohsen Rezaee, career IRGC commander-in-chief now running the security council. Cipher Brief: 'Tehran isn't saying who is actually in charge.' Capped at 82% because the state has promised footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders — that is the falsifier, and it is coming.

hypotheses.name: Nobody’s hurrying on Hormuz — HELD at 60%
hypotheses.d: The near-breakthrough-then-condition pattern fired a sixth time (Iran–Oman interim corridor and 30–60 days of technical talks, against Ghalibaf restating the full condition stack). Deliberately not moved: it is already priced, and a minesweeping calendar is what an honest process looks like too. The real test is live — the offer sits with the IRGC, so Tehran's answer is the experiment.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — 55% → 60%
hypotheses.d: The discriminating split signal arrived: PLA sorties kept declining while the coast guard escalated in kind — CCG 2307 pressing a Japanese coast guard ship in the strait Aug 6–10, which AEI reads as testing whether foreign vessels will obey PRC authority. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up is the ratchet signature. Capped at +5; the stated tell is what the coast guard does through the Sept 24 visit.

hypotheses.name: NEW · Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it opens at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts, and the reporting frames it in plain words as an alternative to Gulf oil routed through Hormuz. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Operation Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Mundane alternative, named and live: drugs, migration politics, regime-change, with the barrel a bonus. Falsifiers — cut hard if export volumes stay token (the $2-2.8bn tranches are a rounding error against control of 65bn bbl), if Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing does not actually swing off the Middle East, or if the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appears. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz, geography does not work that way — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Real Orinoco or Maracaibo channel-dredging and dedicated heavy-crude terminals WOULD be the premeditation tell. Unconfirmed today; it is the thing to watch.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — 45% → 52%
hypotheses.d: Economic Outcast hit ~60 teapots, tankers and traders and touched no Chinese state major and no bank — Treasury sent the majors a warning letter instead. Maximum pressure on Iran, calibrated to stop exactly short of anything that would detonate the Sept 24 summit. Held to +7 because the Munir offer is a real concession, and $4.10 gas before midterms is real evidence against premeditation.

hypotheses.name: NEW · A pre-announcement leak into oil futures
hypotheses.d: Four times in the war window, nine- and ten-figure short bets landed 15–20 minutes before an Iran announcement: ~$2.2bn across crude, gasoil and gasoline before Trump's Mar 23 pause post; ~$950m before the Apr 7 ceasefire; ~$760m before Iran said Hormuz would open. ~$7bn total; CFTC probing, four members of Congress demanding answers. Split: deliberate leak 45 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 25 / coincidence 10. This is the only entry in the book whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event rather than pattern-matched after — which is why it opens this high. Against it: no episode has surfaced around this week's diplomacy.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 30% → 25%
hypotheses.d: Cut again. The channels that actually moved this week were Oman, Pakistan and the new Mecca defence pact — Russia was absent from every one of them, and still has not offered the mediation this hypothesis expects. Motive 9/10, documentary evidence 0/10, pre-event evidence never. Cut to 15% if nothing surfaces by Sept 30.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Both its live predictions came in favourably this week and it gets credit for neither: the rival leverage hypothesis predicted the same things, and shared predictions are ambience. One more failed pre-summit call and it goes to the epitaph list.

brief.h: Trump posted AI-generated video captioned “Kharg Island being blown to smithereens” - hours later there was still no evidence Kharg had been touched, and oil had already paid up 3 percent
brief.t: The real American operation on Sunday was two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak Island, which CENTCOM called “limited, precise” and said it ordered because Revolutionary Guards were readying rockets carrying sea mines for the international shipping lanes. Kharg - the terminal that handles roughly 90 percent of Iran's crude exports - sits more than 400 miles up the Gulf and was not struck; Tehran dismissed the post. Iran answered Larak with ballistic missiles at two US bases in Jordan, eight of which Jordan's military says it intercepted, and a drone at the UAE that the Emirati air force shot down. Brent closed at 90.69 dollars, up 2.93 percent.
brief.context: Name the mechanism: free coercion. A threat only moves markets if it is credible, and this one is credible because it was rehearsed - the US actually bombed Kharg on 13 March 2026, hitting more than 90 military sites on the island while deliberately sparing the oil infrastructure, and Trump has floated seizing the terminal since early July. That history is the rail; the video is the permit it licenses, because a president who has already destroyed the military half of an island can gesture at the commercial half for free. The desks that decide are CENTCOM and the IRGC Navy, not either podium, and both of them behaved with restraint while the loudest object of the day was a rendering. Schelling's distinction is the frame: deterrence is cheap because the other side only has to keep doing nothing, while compellence - stop mining, reopen the strait - demands a visible climb-down and therefore usually fails without a face-saving ladder attached, and none was. Base rate: Pape's survey of twentieth-century strategic air campaigns found that punishment aimed at an economy or a population almost never converts into political concessions, while denial - taking away what an army can physically do - sometimes does; the Larak strike was denial and the Kharg video is punishment theatre. The influence map runs principal Trump, narrator Truth Social, operator CENTCOM, market Brent, target the Iranian treasury - and note that the market paid without the operator doing anything.

angles.effect: Buys an oil-risk premium and a domestic toughness story with no munition, no casualty and no appropriation. Synthetic footage is the cheapest coercive instrument ever available to a head of state, and before a midterm it is cheaper still.

Gets a free credibility win it can point at - intact terminals against a claim of destruction - and an argument at home that American threats are bluff, which makes the next real threat harder to land.

Carry the transfer. A 2.93 percent move on a rendering is real money moving from importers and motorists to holders of length, and US pump prices are already above 4 dollars against under 3 when this war began in February.

angles.party: Allied governments and the verification commons
angles.effect: Pay the long bill. Once a head of state publishes synthetic war footage, every genuine strike image needs authentication before it can deter anyone - the currency of visual proof is being spent down, and allies who must act on US claims are the ones left holding it.

dec.kill: Satellite imagery or an Iranian acknowledgement of actual damage to Kharg's loading terminals within 30 days would make the post a warning order rather than theatre. Terminals intact a month from now, with no strike, confirms the free-coercion read.

brief.h: Bessent says secondary sanctions will now land every week and called it “financial violence” - and again named another bank, and again not a Chinese one
brief.t: The Treasury secretary told the Associated Press he expects to unveil new secondary sanctions weekly, focused initially on banks, and that another bank would be designated this week under the campaign Treasury launched last week as Operation Economic Outcast. “This is going to be financial violence if we have to,” he said. He takes the demand to G20 finance ministers meeting in Asheville, North Carolina on Monday and Tuesday: sever economic ties with Iran or face secondary designation. Bloomberg reported that the world has mostly shrugged off the earlier “D-Day” threat; last week's designation hit Egypt's Banque Misr through its UAE branches.
brief.context: This is a late chapter of the epoch that opened in 2022, when freezing a central bank's reserves converted the settlement system itself into a weapon. Farrell and Newman named the machine: global finance has a hub topology, the hub can both watch and exclude, and the exclusion power - the chokepoint effect - is why an announcement from a Washington podium reorganises a bank's client list in Dubai. But their own caveat is the live question, because chokepoint power decays with each use as targets build alternatives, and China's CIPS was clearing roughly 270 billion dollars a month by March. The desk that actually enforces this is not OFAC but the compliance department of every foreign correspondent bank, which is why a WEEKLY cadence is itself the weapon - it maximises private pre-emptive de-risking per dollar of enforcement. Mulder's rule for sieges applies: a blockade is only as tight as its leakage path, and the leakage path is Chinese purchase, which is precisely who keeps not being designated. Base rate: Hufbauer and colleagues put sanctions success at 5 to 35 percent, and Drezner puts it near zero against a great power on a core interest - which is why our book has the campaign achieving its stated aim at 12 percent. The falsifier is dated: a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank before 24 September would break the hammer-that-hangs read outright.

angles.effect: Gains a signature policy that costs no American lives and no appropriated money before a midterm - the cheapest instrument on the shelf, which is exactly why it is being run at maximum volume.
Do the actual enforcing. The sanction works through private over-compliance, so the cost lands on institutions that were never accused of anything and have no forum to contest it.
The buyer whose behaviour would decide the outcome, still untouched. Every week that passes with a cheap nail hit instead is evidence about what Washington will not pay.

Carry the siege. The rial at a record low, inflation near 70 percent and oil revenue the central bank governor describes as having fallen to zero - and Drezner's finding is that this pain has historically not converted into policy change.
Pay disproportionately. Egypt's Banque Misr is the template: a G20-adjacent institution in a state that cannot answer back is where an instrument gets demonstrated.

dec.kill: A top-ten Chinese bank designated before 24 September, or Chinese customs data showing Iranian crude imports halved for two consecutive months, would mean the siege is biting where it counts and both the leverage read and the 12 percent both go up.

brief.h: Putin, Xi, Modi, Pezeshkian and Erdogan are all in Bishkek - the coalition Brzezinski warned about in 1997 is now holding its 25th-anniversary summit
brief.t: The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit opened in Bishkek on 31 August for two days, marking the bloc's 25th year. Putin is due to meet Xi and Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian separately and Modi on the sidelines; Pakistan's Shehbaz Sharif and Turkey's Erdogan are also there. West Asia, Ukraine, trade, energy and transport connectivity are on the agenda. Modi arrives days after India's April-June growth printed 7.8 percent, beating forecasts.
brief.context: Brzezinski wrote in The Grand Chessboard in 1997 that the one development capable of ending American primacy was an antihegemonic coalition of Russia, China and Iran - and it is the single best long-range structural call in our canon, because that group is now in one room with a logo and an anniversary. Score it honestly, though, because the interesting analysis is the gap between the photograph and the instrument: the SCO has no mutual-defence clause, no common currency, no joint command and no enforcement body, and its two largest members after China fought a border war within living memory. The desk that decides whether this coalition is real is not the summit hall but the People's Bank of China and Chinese customs - the operative question is whether Beijing's purchases of discounted sanctioned barrels from both Moscow and Tehran are priced as solidarity or as leverage, and every quarter of data so far says leverage. India is the tell that keeps the reading sober: Delhi buys Russian crude, American weapons and Gulf gas, and a 7.8 percent growth print is precisely what a state that refuses to pick a bloc looks like when it is winning. Base rate: multipolar bloc summits produce communiques far more often than binding instruments, and the SCO has 25 years of exactly that record. Falsifier: a named operational deliverable - a working non-dollar settlement mechanism, a joint energy facility with committed capital, or any defence clause - would mean this stopped being a photograph and started being an alliance.

brief.h: Russia's Africa Corps helped a junta survive its own soldiers in Niamey - and Moscow's Sahel guarantee just converted from an advertisement into an obligation
brief.t: Mutinous soldiers attacked the presidential palace, the state broadcaster and Airbase 101 in Niger's capital on 29 August. Government forces retook Base 101 with ground and aerial support from Russia's Africa Corps, whose Niger detachment C4ADS puts at 200 to 300 personnel; Russia's ambassador Viktor Voropaev said Nigerien authorities requested the assistance. Algeria separately sent four fighter jets, a transport aircraft and a refuelling tanker. The mutineers are reported to be junior officers drawn from Ouallam, Tera and Dosso, frontline districts where the army has taken heavy casualties against jihadist groups.
brief.context: Start with the runway, not the ideology. Airbase 101 is the field American forces used until the 2024 withdrawal; the same tarmac now hosts the Russian detachment that just decided who governs Niger, which is the rail this headline is a late chapter of. Name the mechanism: regime-preservation as a service. A small deniable detachment is cheap leverage precisely because it is small - but a guarantor that has been publicly asked to fight has bought a commitment it must underwrite next time, and 200 to 300 personnel supplied overland through Burkina Faso does not scale into a garrison. Prefer the boring explanation for the mutiny itself, and it is the likelier one: this reads as a pay-and-body-bags revolt by officers from the worst-hit sectors, not a foreign plot, and the incompetence alternative - a junta that cannot supply its own front - explains the facts without any hidden hand. Base rate: most coup attempts fail, so survival is unremarkable; what is not unremarkable is that a coup-proofed junta needed foreign troops to survive its own army, and the recurrence literature is clear that a first failed attempt materially raises the odds of a second. The file nobody named today sits underneath: Niger's uranium and the European utilities that used to buy it. Watch airlift rather than statements - C4ADS logged only six Russian military flights into Niger across 19 months against 75 into the Sahel overall.

angles.effect: Survives, at the price of owing that survival to a foreign detachment sitting on its own principal airbase - a debt that will be collected in access, minerals or basing rather than in cash.

Gets the best advertisement its Africa Corps could buy, demonstrated live to every other African client. It also acquires a defend-the-palace expectation it cannot meet at current strength if two clients wobble at once.
Buys influence over a neighbour cheaply with four jets and a tanker, and quietly competes with Russia for the same client - the rivalry the headline does not mention and the one to watch.

angles.party: Nigerien soldiers at Ouallam, Tera and Dosso
angles.effect: Pay twice. Their casualties were the grievance, the mutiny failed, and nothing about the way the war is being fought changes - which is the condition under which it happens again.
Carry a risk nobody priced today. The security of a fuel supply chain now depends on a Russian detachment's willingness to keep a junta standing.

dec.kill: A visible burst of Flight Unit 224 or Il-76 movements into Niamey above the six-flight run rate would mark the shift from advisers to garrison and confirm the obligation read. Flat traffic with the junta still standing in a month would mean the assistance was small, local and mostly political.

brief.h: Nepal's flood toll passed 903 dead with 4,247 missing - a glacier fell 1,200 metres into a river and took 72 kilometres of the Trishuli valley with it
brief.t: On 26 August a roughly 600-metre section of glacier near Langtang Lirung collapsed, fell about 1,200 metres and melted from the friction of the impact, triggering a landslide and a flash flood down the Trishuli. It destroyed the Gyirong Port crossing on the China-Nepal border seven minutes after the seismic signal, and struck settlements along a 72-kilometre stretch; some remains were carried 240 kilometres into India. Tibet reports 16 dead and 546 missing. Six hydropower facilities were damaged, taking an estimated 431 megawatts off the grid, and Nepal's preliminary damage estimate is 200 billion rupees, about 1.3 billion dollars. USGS analysis of long-period seismic waves was consistent with a glacier collapse rather than an earthquake.
brief.context: The machine behind this headline is the Himalayan cascade - ice failure into landslide into debris flood - and what makes it strategic rather than only tragic is where the water went. Gyirong is one of the two working road crossings between China and Nepal and the artery of Beijing's overland trade with Kathmandu; the same valley carries the checkpoint, the highway and the dams, because Nepal concentrated its post-2015-earthquake hydropower buildout in exactly this corridor. Follow the money: run-of-river hydro is simultaneously Nepal's principal export ambition and its principal creditor exposure, and debt taken against turbines does not disappear when the turbines do - 431 megawatts and 1.3 billion dollars in a 43-billion-dollar economy is a sovereign balance-sheet event, not a weather story. The desks that decide are Nepal's home ministry and China's border administration, not any foreign ministry. Base rate: this is the same class as Chamoli 2021, Sikkim 2023 and Thame 2024, and the honest finding is not that such events are unforeseeable but that the exposure keeps being rebuilt in the same valleys - the failure is in siting and insurance, not in prediction. Falsifier for the strategic read: if Gyirong reopens within a quarter and Chinese trade volume recovers, this stays a humanitarian disaster; if the crossing is still shut into 2027, Nepal's China option narrows to a single route and Kathmandu's leverage with Delhi falls with it.

lesson: Thomas Schelling's Arms and Influence draws a line that almost every news cycle blurs, and today's board is the cleanest example of it in months. DETERRENCE is telling someone not to start something; it is cheap, because the other side only has to keep doing nothing, and nobody has to be seen backing down. COMPELLENCE is forcing someone to actively stop, undo or hand over something they are already doing — and it is far harder, because it requires a visible climb-down, which is exactly the thing governments cannot afford in front of their own supporters. Schelling's insight was that compellence therefore needs an off-ramp built into the threat: a way for the target to comply that does not look like surrender. Look at what happened here. The Kharg video is a compellent threat — stop mining the strait, reopen it — delivered in a form that gives Tehran no ladder down at all, and the same is true of a weekly sanctions cadence announced in advance, which converts every future pause into a public retreat by the sanctioner. Meanwhile the actual strike was tiny and target-matched, and Iran's reply was fired at forewarned bases and intercepted: both sides operating the deterrence half of the ledger competently while the loud half fails. The falsifiable prediction that follows: over the next three months expect the pattern to hold — small proportionate exchanges that do not escalate, alongside maximal declaratory threats that do not produce Iranian compliance — and if instead Tehran publicly reopens the strait under threat without any face-saving instrument attached, Schelling's rule is failing on this file and we should say so out loud.

lecture.title: The Economic Weapon: Why Sieges Make the Wars They Mean to Prevent

sections.t: Treasury designated roughly sixty Chinese “teapot” refiners — the small plants buying discounted Iranian crude — while touching no Chinese state major and no bank. The same week, central banks bought a record 288.9 tonnes of gold in the quarter gold fell over 20%. Two stories, one machine.

sections.h: Follow the money, name the mechanism
sections.t: A reserve manager buying into a 20% drawdown is not trading. He is hedging ACCESS — the risk that an asset held abroad gets switched off by its host government — and gold is the only large reserve asset with no counterparty who can flip that switch. Name the mechanism: the ECONOMIC WEAPON, using the financial plumbing whose hubs one country owns to inflict a siege without laying one. Iran discounts crude to Chinese teapots paying through dollar-touching chains; Treasury designates them; the IRGC's Strait Authority recoups the shortfall in Hormuz tolls. Sanction and gold bar are one transaction seen from two ends.

sections.h: Deep history I — the blockade that became an idea
sections.t: The economic weapon has a birthday and a founding failure. The birthday is November 1806, when Napoleon's Berlin Decrees declared the British Isles blockaded — the Continental System, an attempt to beat a maritime power by closing a continent's markets to it. It succeeded at nothing except generating enforcement. Portugal would not comply, so France invaded in 1807 and got the Peninsular War, the ulcer that bled the Grande Armée for six years. Alexander I quit the system in December 1810 because it was ruining Russian trade, and in 1812 Napoleon marched east to enforce it. The blockade never defeated Britain; it manufactured the two wars that destroyed the blockader. Sanctions require enforcement, and enforcement against a determined leakage path tends toward conquest. The second case mattered because it worked. The Allied blockade of Germany ran from 1914 through the armistice and was lifted only when Germany signed at Versailles in June 1919. German official estimates put civilian deaths from malnutrition near 424,000 — contested, and historians still argue how much was blockade and how much German agricultural mismanagement. But perception makes policy, and a generation concluded hunger had beaten an undefeated army. So they institutionalized it as a PEACE instrument: Article 16 of the League Covenant made sanctions automatic against an aggressor, and Wilson in 1919 put it in words no Treasury official would dare use today — “A nation that is boycotted is a nation that is in sight of surrender. Apply this economic, peaceful, silent, deadly remedy and there will be no need for force.” The weapon was invented to ABOLISH war; the rest of the century refutes that sentence.

sections.h: Deep history II — the failures that define our problem
sections.t: ABYSSINIA, 1935. Italy invaded Ethiopia; the League invoked Article 16 — exempting oil, coal and steel, and never closing the Suez Canal, which Britain controlled and through which Italian troopships sailed. Mussolini won anyway. The sanctions were real enough to enrage and too porous to stop, and the lesson is sharper than “sanctions don't work”: a sanction calibrated to spare the sender teaches the target that the sender is deterred too. Then the second-order effect. Nicholas Mulder's argument in The Economic Weapon is that the interwar regime deterred small states and PROVOKED large ones. Italy, Germany and Japan drew the same conclusion from the 1930s — dependence on seaborne trade was a vulnerability an enemy could switch off at will, and the answer was autarky, self-sufficiency taken by force. Lebensraum and the Co-Prosperity Sphere were ideological projects; they were also sanctions-proofing programs. Japan is the proof case. Washington embargoed scrap iron in 1940, then froze Japanese assets on 26 July 1941; America supplied roughly 80% of Japan's oil, and with Britain and the Dutch East Indies following, Japan lost about 88% of its oil imports. Reserves would last three years at peace, half that at war — Nagano's image was of a patient wasting away, every month of compliance leaving Japan weaker against the enemy it expected to fight. Pearl Harbor came in December. And the detail that turns story into discipline: the freeze was never meant to be total. Roosevelt intended a licensing regime keeping oil flowing so the tap stayed usable as leverage; officials in State and Treasury administered it so strictly that no licences issued and the flow stopped. The sanction that helped produce Pearl Harbor was substantially an organizational outcome, not a presidential decision — Allison's Essence of Decision, live. Before inferring “Iran's strategy” from one action, ask which bureau took it.

sections.h: The pattern — and where it breaks
sections.t: The leakage path is always the whole story — not the designation list, the leak: Portugal and Russia in 1806, Beira and Pretoria in 1966, Chinese teapots now. NOW THE BREAK. Japan in 1941 had a military option that promised to SOLVE its resource problem: seize the Dutch East Indies and own the oil. Iran has none — it fought its war, lost the conventional exchange, and has played its asymmetric card, the Hormuz toll. Nor did 1914 face an alternative supplier: Iran's is the world's second-largest economy, which the sanctioner just spared. Less Pearl Harbor, more Rhodesia.

MULDER says the siege provokes: strangulation drives large states to autarky, then preemption. DREZNER says sanctions are cheap theater — Hufbauer's data give a third success rate at best, near zero against great powers. The 2026 evidence buries neither: it splits by SIDE, and the split is the finding. On the TARGET Mulder scores: gold, stockpiles, payment rails, enrichment acceleration under maximum pressure. On the SENDER Drezner scores harder — the carve-outs. Sixty teapots and not one bank is not escalation; it is the sanctioner taking its own threat hostage, because hitting a Chinese bank endangers the dollar system that makes the hammer heavy.

The 2015 architecture is not coming back (high confidence): the 2022 freeze of Russian reserves turned the settlement network into an instrument; a hedge once bought is not resold. Expect bifurcation, not de-dollarization (moderate-high). EICHENGREEN is right that currencies erode glacially; the WEAPON depreciates faster than the CURRENCY. The bolder call (moderate): the most dangerous decade is the one in which the weapon still works but no longer terrifies. Mulder's mechanism fires in the transition — invested in escaping, not finished, expecting strangulation regardless. For China, the 2030s — so Economic D-Day may SHORTEN the fuse it was meant to lengthen. FALSIFIER: designate a major Chinese state bank; if Beijing cuts Iranian purchases within a quarter, I am wrong. Two centuries say the economic weapon does not replace war — it sorts the world into blocs that survive each other's sieges, then gives the survivors a reason to fight.
